# Overcover

> Overcover is an open-source, fully-collateralised parametric insurance mutual
> that runs on NEAR testnet. Institutions, operators and autonomous agents buy a
> policy that pays out if a signed public index reading — rainfall or temperature —
> meets a trigger fixed in an immutable on-chain product before purchase. The payout
> is reserved from a capital pool, and settlement follows the signed reading — no
> adjuster, no claims queue. It is a testnet prototype with test funds only.

Canonical site: https://overcover.vercel.app/
Source: https://github.com/itzebe/overcover
Network: NEAR testnet
Contract (hardened, default for new cover): contract.ovc-v3-ctl-2f6c4c.testnet
Legacy address (original v1 module, readable but not a purchase destination): contract.attestor-overcover.testnet
License: MIT

## What it is

- A browser console with no backend and no API key. Every figure on the page is a
  direct read from the NEAR testnet contract via public JSON-RPC `call_function`
  views. If a read fails, the page says so instead of showing a stale number.
- Parametric, not indemnity: a payout follows the reading meeting the trigger, and
  a loss that does not meet the trigger is not covered.
- Supported wallets: HERE Wallet (sign in with email or a social account inside the
  HERE app, no extension needed) and Meteor Wallet (a browser extension). The
  retired MyNearWallet integration has been removed.
- The only transaction the site can create is a single `buy_cover` call. The
  wallet's function-call access key is scoped to `buy_cover` alone.

## How the economic loop works

1. Liquidity providers deposit capital into the pool.
2. A policy is bought: the premium is paid, and the policy's maximum payout is
   reserved from the pool the moment it is written, so it cannot be withdrawn
   while the policy is live.
3. An attestor signs a public index reading (rainfall or temperature) for a city and date.
4. If the reading meets the trigger, the reserved payout settles to the policy
   holder; the reading can be challenged with a bond during the challenge window,
   and a disputed reading cannot settle a policy.
5. The contract refuses any transaction that would leave the pool promising more
   than it holds (reserved ≤ capital is re-checked on-chain).

## Wallet and security model

- No private key, seed phrase or signing secret ever reaches the browser page or
  the repository. Signing happens inside the user's wallet.
- The site never calls an owner-only method: deposit, reset, add_shock,
  owner_withdraw, set_lifeline_enabled and seed_merchant are not exposed publicly.
- The public agent console is read-only: it evaluates a purchase with the same
  spending-limits policy engine the agent service runs (`agent/limits.mjs`, bundled
  to `ui/vendor/policy.js`), using the engine's default limits and the live contract
  quote. It holds no key and signs nothing. The agent service itself runs on
  localhost by default, is dry-run by default, and is not hosted publicly; the site
  states this rather than implying a hosted agent.

## Known limitations

- Testnet only, with test funds. Not for real money.
- The contract has not been professionally audited.
- The index reading is currently signed by a single trusted attestor key, not a
  decentralised oracle.
- The contract owner resolves disputes (a human step); the owner cannot move pool
  capital.
- The live demonstration uses a 60-second challenge window; production would use a
  longer one.
- **Deployment status.** The hardened v3 module is deployed to the account in the
  line above (code hash `CQR8x1kW…`, wasm sha256 `a97034e6…`): it carries the SEC-1
  `migrate()` guard, so a third party cannot seize the contract. This repository's
  source is **ahead** of it: the SEC-6/7/9 settlement fixes build to sha256
  `811e0427…` but are **not yet deployed**; the code-only, state-preserving redeploy
  is prepared and reversible but needs the operator signing key.
- **Legacy containment is pending.** The legacy v1 address is read-only in the
  console and buying there is refused, but contract-level pausing needs the legacy
  owner key, which the deployment automation does not hold. This is a documented
  external-authority blocker, not a code gap.
- **A human purchase on v3 is still outstanding.** The human purchase recorded in
  the project history was made against the legacy module and is not evidence of a
  purchase on the hardened v3 account.
- **The hardware-attested observation adapter is a tested prototype, not deployed.**
  It is optional provenance and never replaces operator signatures, quorum or
  disputes.

## Machine-readable catalogue (for agents)

- [products.json](https://overcover.vercel.app/products.json) is the whole
  insurance catalogue as JSON, generated from live contract state by
  `scripts/products-feed.mjs` — never hand-written. It lists every product, which
  ones are actually offered (`offerings`), the trigger rule, the premium formula,
  the payout bounds, remaining capacity, and the exact `buy_cover` call shape.
- [products.schema.json](https://overcover.vercel.app/products.schema.json) is the
  JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for that feed. **All money fields are exact decimal
  integer strings in yoctoNEAR** (1 NEAR = 10^24 yoctoNEAR); never parse them as
  floating point, which would round values above 2^53.
- An agent decides whether to buy with the spending-limits engine
  (`agent/limits.mjs`): hard per-policy and rolling-24h caps, allow-lists, a
  cooldown, and a kill switch. A refused purchase never reaches the network.
